# Requirements

Replace agent-owned provider setup with an independent, standalone model gateway inspired by an examined and pinned 9router architecture. Agents and other applications consume its standard inference endpoint.

## Requirement 1: Independent subsystem and source-grounded reference

**User Story:** As an operator, I can use the model gateway without creating or running an agent.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Inspect pinned 9router source, document actual persistence/authentication/executor/translator/routing boundaries and license; separate supported formats from provider-specific sign-in flows.
2. model_gateway imports neither agent nor consumer; owns durable state, encryption, API keys, routing and usage; runs through its own CLI/ASGI app or composition mount.

## Requirement 2: Provider connections and current catalogs

**User Story:** As a self-hosted user, I connect a preset or custom provider in one drawer.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Preset provider name and endpoint, inline encrypted API key, bounded live model discovery/import and optional custom model IDs replace credential references, required token-limit fields and manual probe/activate steps.
2. Include source-backed free/no-auth, free-tier, local, paid and compatible gateway presets; label account quotas and specialized authentication honestly; support custom endpoints for implemented wire formats.
3. Connections support multiple accounts, optimistic revisions, refresh, update and disconnect; secrets never enter frontend persistence, public responses, logs or usage records.

## Requirement 3: Inference gateway and routing

**User Story:** As any model client, I connect once and use imported models or named routes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Authenticated OpenAI-compatible models and chat completions work in streaming and nonstreaming modes; upstream OpenAI Chat, Responses, Anthropic and Gemini translation supports arbitrary function names, usage, cancellation and honest terminal states.
2. Named priority and round-robin routes provide bounded fallback before output, retryable-failure cooldowns and usage for each attempt; no retry after visible output and no invented usage.
3. Client keys are hashed, revocable and model-scoped; tenant authority is server-derived; network destinations and local-server exceptions remain bounded and isolated from agent tool policy.

## Requirement 4: Independent premium management and agent client

**User Story:** As a user, I manage model infrastructure separately and select a gateway model for my agent.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Material 3 Model Gateway navigation works before an agent exists and while agent runtimes are stopped, with provider search, connection drawer, model import, routes, keys and usage.
2. Agent settings choose a gateway model through one action; only a restricted gateway credential reaches its runtime; upstream provider keys remain gateway-owned. Existing configurations and user data survive migration.
3. Exercise real browser setup, model import, key creation and agent model binding against controlled wire servers; rebuild and restart the authorized local service after qualification.

## Requirement 5: Documentation and qualification

**User Story:** As a user or developer, I can learn and operate every gateway feature with examples.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Both documentation sites include gateway setup, free-tier limits, local/custom providers, model discovery, keys, routes, troubleshooting, standalone operation, architecture, all source references and boundaries.
2. Preserve full Python/C++/client 90 percent executable-line floors; include model_gateway in production and documentation inventories, run full documentation gate, and report live vendor qualification separately from controlled wire proof.
